review_scope: One production-file, two-hunk candidate; parent admission, intercepted policy fallback, explicit rule/dangerous/Granular enforcement, and sandbox execution ownership. No Rust or external command execution.

findings.conclusion: Parent policy admission precedes the only production provider construction; RequireEscalated is not treated as a grant by itself.

source_chain.fact: The actual runtime owner computes the original ExecApprovalRequirement and invokes ToolOrchestrator::run.
Forbidden returns; NeedsApproval and strict-auto-review Skip await request_approval with ? before the first attempt.
run_attempt is invoked after the approval block.
run_attempt invokes the runtime run method after network approval setup.
Zsh preparation is reached from the admitted runtime run path with the actual transformed exec_request.
The Unix wrapper forwards directly to the one production provider constructor.

findings.qualification: Passing the gate includes policy-authorized Skip; this does not assert every request required a separate user prompt.

findings.conclusion: The changed value is solely the policy fallback sandbox classification, derived with the same pre-existing denied-read helper used for parent launch.

source_chain.fact: The helper keeps denied-read restrictions inside the sandbox instead of requesting a bypass.
Parent launch already uses this helper against the effective runtime filesystem policy.
Only approval_sandbox_permissions input changes; raw sandbox_permissions and permission_profile are retained.

findings.conclusion: Explicit prefix rules and dangerous-command checks retain their original priority. An admitted parent does not suppress an explicit child Prompt or Forbidden.

source_chain.fact: The normalized field reaches the unmatched fallback; policy.check_multiple_with_options still evaluates matched prefix rules.
Dangerous-command and Windows unprotected-filesystem checks return Prompt/Forbidden before examining the fallback override flag.
Granular rules and sandbox branches remain distinct and unchanged.
Forbidden still denies; Prompt still traverses the policy gate and review decision before any run/escalation.

findings.conclusion: Execution authority and denied-read enforcement are unchanged.

source_chain.fact: needs_escalation and shell_request_escalation_execution still use the raw request and original profile; denied-read profiles continue to prohibit Unsandboxed.
RequireEscalated returns TurnDefault when unsandboxed_execution_allowed is false.

findings.conclusion: The original direct-constructor rejection test remains meaningful and unchanged; normalization is confined to the production constructor reached after admission.

source_chain.fact: denied_reads_keep_granular_sandbox_rejection_for_escalation still supplies raw RequireEscalated and asserts Deny.

findings.integration_regression: unified_exec_zsh_fork_parent_approval_preserves_denied_reads keeps the parent approval, no-second-approval condition, nonzero exit, and secret-absence assertions.

limitations: Static source review only, not an executed authorization or sandbox guarantee.
No new runtime or helper tests were run by this reviewer.
Native strict/full gate and the unchanged denied-read integration test remain required.
This review does not alter approval policy or endorse general removal of unmatched-command prompts outside the admitted parent path.
